changes: Remove Playwright default --disable-back-forward-cache only, retaining default browser cache and existing proxy/egress constraints.
Passive native pageshow/pagehide events include persisted/isTrusted, path-only location, document/page identity and timestamp.
Capture current native navigation type and reason strings, plus navigation response no-store/cache-control; no URL query, response bytes, cookie or token logging.
Use commit for back/forward navigation and document readiness/render observations before reload.
Explicitly distinguish observed native BFCache restoration from ordinary history navigation or ineligibility/not-used.

Native pageshow records only a private synthetic item presence boolean before later redirect/revalidation as an observation. Event-start DOM alone does not fail a gate; settled post-navigation render and response checks determine failures. Browser version retained.
review_note: Independent reviewer required transient pageshow canaries be observations, not instantaneous DOM-erasure assertions. Applied before admission. Historical navigation Response bodies are retained as observations only because Playwright may expose the original authorized Response on a BFCache hit. The separate actual next-read request and settled DOM assertions remain decisive. Persisted classification is scoped to the actual navigation start timestamp.
